text:
maria: FYI I finished a quick SmoothQuant (activation-aware) sweep vs FP8/INT8/GPTQ on the 13B long-context build (64k tokens). posting notes and raw numbers below.

maria: setup - eval set is longctx-qa-3k (mix of long-form QA and summarization slices up to 64k). baseline = FP16 reference. quant configs: FP8 (e8m1-like auto range + smooth alpha=0.25), AWQ-INT8 per-channel, GPTQ-4bit post-train.

dylan: nice — what's the top-level accuracy delta vs FP16?

maria: short table (EM = exact match on our QA set, lower is worse):

| config     | EM delta vs FP16 | avg perplexity delta | notes |
|------------|------------------:|---------------------:|-------|
| FP16       | 0.0%              | 0.0                  | reference |
| AWQ-INT8   | -1.1%             | +0.7                 | stable across prompts |
| FP8-sq     | -3.4%             | +2.2                 | underperforms on tail long queries |
| GPTQ-4bit  | -5.8%             | +4.8                 | large regressions on numeric answers |

maria: perf (measured on dedicated A100-like pool, batch=1, typical longctx load)
- AWQ-INT8: throughput +1.6x vs FP16, p99 latency ~ 1.12x FP16
- FP8-sq: throughput +2.1x, p99 latency ~ 1.35x FP16 (more variability)
- GPTQ-4bit: throughput +2.8x, p99 latency ~ 1.5x FP16

sasha: FP8 has higher variability — did you see any KV-cache related regressions at 64k?

maria: yes, FP8-sq shows higher activation clipping in later layers when KV cache grows. two things stood out:
1) attention head 5 and layernorm scale drift = main source of EM loss (noticed big per-layer activation tails).
2) dynamic range adapts poorly for tokens after ~32k without per-layer recalibration.

anita: can you share the exact SmoothQuant params you used? alpha, scaling, blocksize?

maria: config snippet:
```
quant_backend: smoothquant
activation_alpha: 0.25
weight_quant: int8
activation_quant: fp8
block_size: 128
calib_samples: 512
per_channel: true
kv_cache_scale: 1.08  # small boost to reduce fp8 saturation in later layers
```

leo: ci artifacts? logs? would help to reproduce.

ci-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/quant-sweeps/1772301120/sq_longctx_fp8_awq.tar.gz :white_check_mark:

dylan: interesting that AWQ-INT8 keeps quality much closer to FP16 with less perf variability. any thoughts on why AWQ beats FP8 on longctx?

maria: hypothesis: AWQ's per-channel scaling + selective outlier handling handles activation tails from cross-attention better. FP8's shared exponent mechanics and smoother quantization amplify rare large activations, so EM suffers on questions that rely on late tokens.

anita: mitigation ideas? per-layer clamping, higher calib samples, or hybrid scheme?

maria: tried quick mitigations: increasing calib_samples -> 1024 reduced FP8 EM delta from -3.4% to -2.1%, adding per-layer clamp for top-3 offending layers -> further to -1.5%. Hybrid approach (FP8 for most layers + AWQ-INT8 on attention + head outliers kept in FP16) -> EM delta -0.6% and throughput +1.9x.

sasha: can you paste the run command you used for the hybrid? want to queue a perf run on perf pool.

maria: run command (toy):
```bash
./rwinf-cli run --model redwood/13B-longctx --quant hybrid --hybrid-layers 'attn:fp16,mlp:int8,rest:fp8' \
  --smooth-alpha 0.25 --calib-samples 1024 --kv-scale 1.08 --context 65536 --batch 1 \
  --eval-set s3://datasets/longctx-qa-3k --output ./runs/1772301120_hybrid
```

dylan: perfect — thank you. will kick off a repeat with longer eval and 3 seeds.

maria: plan: run full hybrid sweep (3 seeds) + AWQ-INT8 refine -> propose default deployment profile: AWQ-INT8 for time-critical routes, hybrid for highest-quality longctx endpoints, FP8-only as opt-in experimental for noncritical batch jobs.

anita: sounds good. add this to the model-onboarding doc and tag infra for rollout notes. :thumbsup:

maria: adding notes now. tagging @dylan @sasha for follow ups.
